reference.source: BAD Guidelines / British Association of Dermatologists / Rook's Dermatology
clinicalPearls: Distal and lateral subungual onychomycosis is the most common clinical presentation, typically caused by Trichophyton rubrum
Features include subungual hyperkeratosis, yellow-brown nail plate discolouration, crumbling, and onycholysis
Nail clippings and subungual scrapings must be sent for direct microscopy (KOH mount) and fungal culture or PCR prior to starting oral antifungal therapy
Psoriatic nail disease closely mimics onychomycosis, displaying pitting, oil-drop/salmon patches, and splinter haemorrhages
Oral terbinafine is the first-line systemic treatment for dermatophyte onychomycosis, requiring treatment for 6 weeks (fingernails) to 12 weeks (toenails)
Baseline liver function tests are recommended prior to systemic antifungal therapy, with monitoring during prolonged courses
Topical nail lacquers (amorolfine, ciclopirox) are reserved for superficial white onychomycosis or mild distal involvement of fewer than two nails
reference.pathophysiology: Onychomycosis is a fungal infection of the nail unit involving the nail bed, matrix, or plate. Dermatophytes (principally Trichophyton rubrum and Trichophyton mentagrophytes) account for approximately ninety percent of toenail infections, with non-dermatophyte moulds (Scopulariopsis, Fusarium) and yeasts (Candida albicans) causing a minority. Fungal hyphae invade keratinised nail structures, producing subungual hyperkeratosis, architectural distortion, and separation of the nail plate from the underlying vascular nail bed.
additionalDifferentials: Nail psoriasis (pitting, oil-drop salmon patches, onycholysis with red border)
Lichen planus of the nail (longitudinal ridging, pterygium unguis)
Yellow nail syndrome (absent lunula, thick yellow nails, lymphedema, bronchiectasis)
additionalInvestigations: Nail clippings from the most proximal involved dystrophic area and subungual debris curettage
Potassium hydroxide (KOH) wet mount or calcofluor white fluorescent microscopy
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar with cycloheximide to identify species
Fungal PCR for rapid identification of dermatophyte DNA
Baseline liver enzymes (ALT, AST) before oral terbinafine or itraconazole
